transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-27 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (CTO, Switchboard), Jae Park (Head of ML), Maria Lopez (Infra), Anika Bose (Product), Speaker 6

Summary: Quick intro, high-level posture: Switchboard is evaluating hosted initially but has strict SLAs, exploring dedicated for predictable unit cost. Main focus on per-token unit economics, batching/caching levers, and pilot scope for fraud-detection feature.

---- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ----
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin? we'll do intro then jump into the cost side and tradeoffs, is that right Ravi?
[00:08] Ravi: yeah thanks Samir, appreciate it. quick background — Switchboard is a payments orchestration layer, latency sensitive, 75ms median on auth path today. exploring adding LLM for contextual risk signals, probably 30M requests/month if pilot scales.
[00:25] Lena: cool, and hi Jae, Maria; just to set expectations i want to cover per-token pricing, batching, kv/prefix caching, and what Dedicated or Private might buy you versus Hosted.
[00:40] Jae: when you say per-token pricing, do you mean for generation only or also embeddings? we'll need both for the scoring side.
[00:46] Samir: good call — for this call let's focus mostly on generation and short-context scoring. embeddings pricing is separate and more per-vector, we can add later.
[01:10] Maria: just to flag infra constraints — we need to keep data in eu-west for regulatory reasons, and any private deployment would have to integrate with our KMS and current VPC peering.
[01:20] Lena: noted. Switchboard residency + KMS is a common constraint; Redwood Private supports customer KMS and VPC peering, Dedicated can be placed in region and we can attach dedicated transit.
[01:35] Ravi: ok, show me numbers — rough hosted per-token and what Dedicated changes.
[01:40] Samir: sure. ballpark hosted generation rate we've been quoting is $0.0009 per token for large-family models (this includes infra and managed ops). For Dedicated we typically model a TCO and show per-token falling to ~ $0.00018–$0.00035 depending on utilization, batching, and quantization.
[02:05] Speaker 6 (interrupt): sorry can you repeat that, those ranges look wide.
[02:10] Samir: yeah absolutely. the main drivers: model family (size), quantization level (4-bit vs 8-bit), average response length, and more importantly utilization — Dedicated has fixed monthly cost spread over tokens. at low volume hosted is simpler, at higher volume dedicated often wins.
[02:36] Jae: what's the assumed batching in your Dedicated TCO? we run many short requests (10–30 tokens).
[02:43] Lena: our TCO example assumes continuous batching with micro-batch windows and prefix caching. effective batch size for small responses tends to be 6–12 on average if traffic is bursty and you allow 25–40ms batching window; that reduces per-token compute substantially. If you can't batch (strict 20ms P99), then you won't see the same gains.
[03:10] Maria: we need sub-200ms tail; 95th we can tolerate 350ms sometimes. what's your latency on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:17] Samir: Hosted usually hits 95th around 300–400ms for standard models, but we have low-latency configs too. Dedicated colocated and tuned models can hit 95th < 200ms depending on model/instance class and KV cache hotness.
[03:36] Ravi: hotness?
[03:38] Lena: yeah, KV cache hotness — if you reuse prefixes or keep chat state hot, subsequent requests avoid recompute and are much cheaper. but for stateless, cold requests you pay full token cost.
[03:50] Ravi: got it. can you give me a worked example?
[03:52] Samir: sure — assume 10k requests/day, average 30 input tokens + 20 generated tokens = 50 tokens per request -> 500k tokens/day, 15M tokens/month. Hosted at $0.0009/token -> $13,500/month.
[04:10] Samir: Dedicated: say we reserve a pod equivalent to 8xA100 class, cost to you $20k/month (example commit). with batching and cache we could get effective unit cost to $0.00025/token — that'd be about $3,750/month equivalent, so big delta. But commitment and utilization matters.
[04:35] Jae: those numbers assume 100% utilization?
[04:38] Lena: no, they assume 60–70% effective utilization across peak windows; lower utilization pushes Hosted back into parity.
[04:44] Anika: what's the break-even point? at what token volume do you recommend moving from Hosted to Dedicated?
[04:50] Samir: rule of thumb — above ~30–50M tokens/month Dedicated often beats Hosted, but depends on your acceptable commit and SLA. for Switchboard's 30M projected, you're around the cusp.
[05:05] Maria: we might see bursty spikes during peak shopping times, any auto-fallbacks?
[05:10] Lena: yes — Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies: Dedicated primary, Hosted fallback for overflow. we can also set cost-based routing so non-critical paths go to cheaper variants.
[05:25] Ravi: ok. how about quantization — can you run our model 4-bit and still preserve quality?
[05:30] Lena: we often recommend 4-bit quant with awareness that some tasks degrade. we do evals with your prompts to measure quality impact. 4-bit plus pruning + distillation in our Optimize recommendations can give 30–50% speedups.
[05:50] Jae: we'd also be interested in route-level controls — like if a route needs higher quality vs low-latency cheap path. can we split?
[05:56] Samir: absolutely — per-route model pinning and rollout controls. you can route high-criticality auth requests to low-latency Dedicated path and analytics batch jobs to cheaper quantized variants.
[06:15] Speaker 6: quick question on embeddings pricing?
[06:17] Samir: embeddings are billed differently — per-embedding vector and storage for indexes; we'll include that in the spreadsheet but not the focus here.
[06:25] Ravi: curious about cold-start — if we have a hot cache for a user session, do you keep the KV cache across requests?
[06:31] Lena: yes, KV cache persists per session in Dedicated, and Hosted has session caching too but with shorter TTL depending on tenant isolation. long-lived sessions reduce compute by avoiding repeated attention recompute.
[06:45] Jae: one more heavy topic — compliance. we need audit logs, SSO, RBAC, and ideally SOC2+ISO. what's Redwood's posture?
[06:55] Samir: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, supports SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit logs; Private gives you maximum control, including HSM/KMS integration and air-gapped options for extreme cases.
[07:10] Maria: are backups and logs stored in the region? we cannot have logs leave eu-west.
[07:15] Lena: for Private we can ensure logs stay in-region. for Hosted we have region-specific deployments; we can guarantee data residency with contractual terms for enterprise. we'll follow up with the security binder.
[07:30] Ravi: operationally, what does a pilot look like? three month pilot, sandbox dataset, run dual-write to production?
[07:37] Samir: typical pilot: 4–8 weeks technical pilot with 1–2M tokens, then a staged canary in prod. we can do a POC on Hosted first to validate quality then move to Dedicated for cost eval.
[07:52] Anika: timeline: we want to be live for fraud feature by Feb 2027. is that feasible?
[07:56] Lena: feasible — pilot now, evaluation, if you choose Dedicated we recommend a November sizing/contract sign to hit Feb rollout.
[08:05] Jae: demo request: can you show routing + per-route SLA controls in the console next call?
[08:10] Samir: yes. we'll schedule a console demo and an SE-led perf deep dive.
[08:16] Speaker 6: small nit — your earlier pricing mentioned $0.0009 hosted. that's higher than some vendors, why?
[08:22] Samir: our hosted price reflects production SLA, 24/7 ops, model tuning, and integrated caching/batching. some vendors advertise lower sticker rates but then you pay for infra/engineering or face higher latency. we try to be transparent with TCO modeling.
[08:40] Ravi: can you share the assumptions in that TCO model? CPU/GPU hours, license, ops?
[08:45] Lena: yes — we'll share a breakdown: GPU hours, reserved instance cost, orchestration & monitoring overhead, redundancy, and typical utilization. we also surface sensitivity to batch window and quantization.
[08:58] Samir: i'd like to walk through a sensitivity quickly: if average response size doubles, tokens double and Hosted cost doubles, Dedicated still amortizes to a degree but absolute spend goes up. if you tighten latency to 50ms p99, batching is limited and Dedicated may need higher-end instances.
[09:20] Jae: what's a realistic batch delay we can accept? our auth path can't add >60ms.
[09:25] Lena: you could accept 20–25ms micro-batching and still hit ~200ms p95 in Dedicated; it's a tradeoff. some customers allow micro-batch delay only on non-blocking paths.
[09:40] Maria: any numbers on token-per-second throughput on the 8xA100 example?
[09:44] Lena: rough ballpark: for a 13B family model in quantized config you might see 200–700 tokens/sec depending on optimizations. exact numbers need our benchmark with your prompt set.
[09:58] Ravi: let's talk about hybrid — we want Dedicated for auth but Hosted fallback makes sense. how does billing work with that hybrid design?
[10:05] Samir: billing is usage-based. Dedicated is a committed monthly charge; Hosted is pay-as-you-go. if you overflow to Hosted, you pay the Hosted per-token for overflow. we can model blended unit price for forecasting.
[10:18] Anika: can you do per-route cost dashboards?
[10:21] Lena: yes, Redwood Console gives per-route token counts, per-model cost, latency histograms, and tracing tags for request sampling.
[10:30] Speaker 6: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[10:33] Samir: Dedicated SLAs are available as part of reserved capacity contracts, typically 99.9% and quicker response for capacity issues. Hosted has standard SLA tiers.
[10:44] Jae: one operational question — how do we handle model versions? if we pin a model in production and Redwood upgrades, do we get auto-updates?
[10:52] Lena: you can pin a version and control rollouts. auto-updates won't happen without your config. we support canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to older model if regressions detected.
[11:05] Ravi: ok, final quick thing — what should we send you to get an accurate TCO?
[11:09] Samir: we need: projected tokens/month (by route), average tokens per request, P95 latency requirement per route, acceptable batch delay, retention & residency rules, and a sample prompt set (2–3k). also any security reqs.
[11:22] Maria: we'll assemble that.
[11:25] Samir: perfect. i'll send the TCO spreadsheet and a proposed pilot plan. Lena will run the benchmark if you share sample prompts and allow ephemeral test keys.
[11:36] Jae: one last question — do you support private deploy with offline airgapped option? we've got a partner that sometimes wants completely isolated stack.
[11:43] Lena: yes, Private can be packaged for air-gapped, though ops overhead and price increase. we handle key exchanges and can run an on-prem package.
[11:50] Ravi: great. any blockers?
[11:52] Anika: timeline alignment and security review. once we get the security binder we'll route to procurement.
[11:58] Samir: i'll follow up with security docs and SOC2 report.
[12:02] Speaker 6: thanks everyone.

(brief crosstalk and wrap)

Recap & Next Steps (spoken):
- Redwood to send detailed hosted vs dedicated TCO spreadsheet + assumptions (Samir)
- SE to run micro-benchmark on Dedicated-like config using Switchboard prompts (Lena)
- Switchboard to share prompt set, retention rules, and SOC2 contact (Ravi/Maria)
- Schedule console demo + SE deep dive (Samir)

End of meeting.
